- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Software Requirements Specification (SRS)
2	## Rental Management System for IT Equipment Rental Services
3	
4	**Version:** 1.0  
5	**Date:** 2026-07-02  
6	**Prepared For:** Rental Services Business  
7	**Prepared By:** Claude Code  
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Table of Contents
12	1. [Introduction](#1-introduction)
13	   - 1.1 Purpose
14	   - 1.2 Scope
15	   - 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
16	   - 1.4 References
17	   - 1.5 Overview
18	2. [Overall Description](#2-overall-description)
19	   - 2.1 Product Perspective
20	   - 2.2 Product Functions
21	   - 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
22	   - 2.4 Operating Environment
23	   - 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
24	   - 2.6 User Documentation
25	   - 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
26	3. [Specific Requirements](#3-specific-requirements)
27	   - 3.1 External Interface Requirements
28	   - 3.2 Functional Requirements
29	   - 3.3 Non-Functional Requirements
30	   - 3.4 Other Requirements
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. Introduction
35	
36	### 1.1 Purpose
37	This document specifies the software requirements for a Rental Management System (RMS) designed specifically for an IT equipment rental services business. The system will manage the rental operations for servers, laptops, computers, firewalls, printers, and refurbished IT equipment serving business customers including IT companies, manufacturing firms, startups, educational institutions, and BPOs/call centers.
38	
39	### 1.2 Scope
40	The Rental Management System will provide:
41	- Inventory management for all rental equipment
42	- Customer and contract management
43	- Rental transaction processing
44	- Billing and invoicing
45	- Maintenance and repair tracking
46	- Reporting and analytics
47	- Integration with the existing customer-facing website
48	- User role-based access control
49	
50	The system will **not** serve individual consumers; it is strictly for business-to-business (B2B) transactions.
51	
52	### 1.3 Definitions, Acronyms, and Abbreviations
53	
54	| Term | Definition |
55	|------|------------|
56	| RMS | Rental Management System |
57	| B2B | Business-to-Business |
58	| CRM | Customer Relationship Management |
59	| ERP | Enterprise Resource Planning |
60	| SLA | Service Level Agreement |
61	| OEM | Original Equipment Manufacturer |
62	| SLA | Service Level Agreement |
63	
64	### 1.4 References
65	- [IEEE 830-1998] IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications
66	- Existing website: `index.html`, `style.css`, `main.js`
67	- Brand assets: `icons/` directory containing brand logos
68	
69	### 1.5 Overview
70	The remainder of this document describes the overall description of the product (Section 2) and the specific requirements (Section 3) including external interfaces, functional requirements, non-functional requirements, and other requirements.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 2. Overall Description
75	
76	### 2.1 Product Perspective
77	The Rental Management System is a web-based application designed to operate as the backend system for the rental services business. It will integrate with the existing customer-facing website (currently at `index.html`) to provide real-time inventory availability, rental requests, and customer account management.
78	
79	The system will be a multi-user application accessible via web browsers, with different interfaces for administrators, staff, and customers (via portal access).
80	
81	### 2.2 Product Functions
82	The RMS will provide the following core functions:
83	1. **Inventory Management** - Track all rental equipment by type, brand, model, serial number, condition, and availability
84	2. **Customer Management** - Maintain B2B customer profiles, contact information, rental history, and credit terms
85	3. **Rental Management** - Handle rental requests, quotations, contracts, equipment allocation, pickup/delivery scheduling, and returns
86	4. **Billing and Invoicing** - Generate invoices, process payments, track overdue payments, and manage security deposits
87	5. **Maintenance Management** - Track equipment maintenance, repairs, servicing schedules, and warranty claims
88	6. **Reporting and Analytics** - Generate reports on utilization, revenue, customer analytics, and inventory performance
89	7. **Customer Portal** - Allow customers to browse inventory, request rentals, view active rentals, and make payments
90	8. **Integration** - Synchronize with the existing website to display real-time availability and product information
91	
92	### 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
93	
94	| User Type | Characteristics | Permissions |
95	|-----------|----------------|-------------|
96	| **System Administrator** | IT staff responsible for system configuration, user management, and system maintenance | Full system access including user management, system configuration, and all business functions |
97	| **Rental Manager** | Business users managing rental operations, inventory, and customer relationships | Full access to rental, inventory, customer, and billing functions; limited system administration |
98	| **Sales Representative** | Staff handling customer inquiries, quotations, and rental agreements | Access to customer management, rental quotations, and contract creation |
99	| **Operations Staff** | Personnel handling equipment preparation, delivery, pickup, and maintenance | Access to inventory management, equipment status updates, and maintenance scheduling |
100	| **Accounting/Finance** | Staff handling invoicing, payments, and financial reporting | Access to billing, invoicing, payment processing, and financial reports |
101	| **Customer Portal User** | Authorized representatives from B2B customers | Browse inventory, submit rental requests, view active rentals, download invoices, and make payments |
102	
103	### 2.4 Operating Environment
104	- **Web Application:** Browser-based interface accessible via modern browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
105	- **Deployment:** Web server (Apache/Nginx) with application server (Node.js/PHP/Python)
106	- **Database:** Relational database (MySQL/PostgreSQL/MariaDB)
107	- **Integration:** RESTful API for integration with existing website
108	- **Security:** HTTPS encryption, role-based access control, input validation
109	- **Compatibility:** Responsive design for desktop and tablet use
110	
111	### 2.5 Design and Implementation Constraints
112	1. **Integration Constraint:** Must integrate seamlessly with the existing website at `index.html`
113	2. **Technology Stack:** Should leverage existing web technologies where possible (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript)
114	3. **Data Migration:** Must accommodate import of existing inventory and customer data
115	4. **Brand Compliance:** Must comply with brand guidelines for all displayed OEM logos and product information
116	5. **Business Rules:** Must enforce B2B-only rental policy (no individual consumers)
117	6. **Regulatory:** Must comply with data protection regulations for customer information
118	
119	### 2.6 User Documentation
120	- Administrator Guide
121	- Staff User Manual
122	- Customer Portal Guide
123	- API Documentation for website integration
124	- Troubleshooting FAQ
125	
126	### 2.7 Assumptions and Dependencies
127	1. The existing website will remain as the primary customer-facing interface
128	2. The RMS will provide APIs for the website to consume inventory and rental data
129	3. All customers are verified business entities (no individual consumers)
130	4. Initial inventory data will be migrated from existing records
131	5. The system will operate in a single timezone (IST - India Standard Time)
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 3. Specific Requirements
136	
137	### 3.1 External Interface Requirements
138	
139	#### 3.1.1 User Interfaces
140	- **Administrator Dashboard:** Web-based interface for system configuration and oversight
141	- **Staff Interface:** Web-based interface for rental operations, inventory management, and customer service
142	- **Customer Portal:** Secure web interface for customers to browse inventory, request rentals, and manage accounts
143	- **Responsive Design:** All interfaces must be responsive and accessible on desktop and tablet devices
144	- **Brand Consistency:** UI must align with the visual identity of the existing website
145	
146	#### 3.1.2 Hardware Interfaces
147	- Barcode/RFID scanners for inventory tracking (optional)
148	- Receipt printers for on-site transactions
149	- Signature capture devices for delivery confirmations (optional)
150	
151	#### 3.1.3 Software Interfaces
152	- **RESTful API:** For integration with the existing website to provide:
153	  - Real-time inventory availability
154	  - Product catalog information
155	  - Rental request submission
156	  - Customer account information (read-only for website)
157	- **Database:** MySQL 8.0+ or PostgreSQL 12+
158	- **Authentication:** Integration with LDAP/Active Directory optional for internal users
159	- **Payment Gateway:** Integration with payment processors (Stripe, Razorpay, PayPal) for online payments
160	- **Email Service:** Integration with SMTP service for automated notifications (SendGrid, AWS SES, etc.)
161	
162	#### 3.1.4 Communications Interfaces
163	- HTTP/HTTPS for web interfaces
164	- REST/JSON for API communications
165	- SMTP for email notifications
166	- SMS gateway integration optional for SMS notifications
167	
168	### 3.2 Functional Requirements
169	
170	#### 3.2.1 User Management
171	| ID | Requirement Description |
172	|----|------------------------|
173	| UM-001 | The system shall support role-based access control with predefined roles: Administrator, Rental Manager, Sales Representative, Operations Staff, Accounting/Finance |
174	| UM-002 | The system shall allow administrators to create, modify, deactivate, and reactivate user accounts |
175	| UM-003 | The system shall enforce strong password policies (minimum 8 characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters) |
176	| UM-004 | The system shall support multi-factor authentication for administrator accounts |
177	| UM-005 | The system shall log all user login/logout activities and significant actions |
178	| UM-006 | The system shall support password reset functionality via email verification |
179	
180	#### 3.2.2 Inventory Management
181	| ID | Requirement Description |
182	|----|------------------------|
183	| IM-001 | The system shall track inventory items with attributes: item ID, type (server/laptop/computer/firewall/printer/refurbished), brand, model, serial number, specifications, acquisition date, warranty information, condition (new/refurbished), location, and status (available/rented/maintenance/reserved) |
184	| IM-002 | The system shall support categorization of inventory by all major brands (Dell, HP, Lenovo, IBM, Asus, Acer, Canon, Cisco, Fortinet, Sophos, etc.) |
185	| IM-003 | The system shall track refurbished equipment separately with certification details and warranty information |
186	| IM-004 | The system shall allow bulk import of inventory data via CSV/Excel |
187	| IM-005 | The system shall generate unique identification numbers/tags for each inventory item |
188	| IM-006 | The system shall track equipment location (warehouse, customer site, in-transit, maintenance) |
189	| IM-007 | The system shall automate status updates based on rental transactions (rented → available upon return) |
190	| IM-008 | The system shall support barcode/QR code generation for inventory tracking |
191	| IM-009 | The system shall prevent rental of equipment under maintenance or repair |
192	
193	#### 3.2.3 Customer Management
194	| ID | Requirement Description |
195	|----|------------------------|
196	| CM-001 | The system shall maintain customer profiles with: company name, contact person, email, phone, address, GST/VAT number, industry type (IT/manufacturing/business/startup/educational/BPO), credit limit, payment terms |
197	| CM-002 | The system shall validate that all customers are business entities (no individual consumers allowed) |
198	| CM-003 | The system shall track customer rental history, including all past and current rentals |
199	| CM-004 | The system shall allow categorization of customers by industry vertical for reporting purposes |
200	| CM-005 | The system shall store multiple contacts per customer account |
201	| CM-006 | The system shall flag customers with overdue payments or excessive late returns |
202	| CM-007 | The system shall support customer self-registration with admin approval workflow |
203	
204	#### 3.2.4 Rental Management
205	| ID | Requirement Description |
206	|----|------------------------|
207	| RM-001 | The system shall allow customers to browse available inventory through the customer portal or website |
208	| RM-002 | The system shall allow customers to submit rental requests specifying equipment, quantities, rental period, delivery/pickup preferences |
209	| RM-003 | The system shall allow staff to create rental quotations based on customer requirements |
210	| RM-004 | The system shall generate rental agreements/contracts with terms and conditions, pricing, and SLA details |
211	| RM-005 | The system shall track rental equipment allocation to specific customer orders |
212	| RM-006 | The system shall schedule and track equipment delivery and pickup logistics |
213	| RM-007 | The system shall support rental extensions and early terminations with prorated billing |
214	| RM-008 | The system shall enforce minimum and maximum rental periods based on equipment type |
215	| RM-009 | The system shall require security deposits for high-value equipment (servers, enterprise equipment) |
216	| RM-010 | The system shall automate equipment readiness checks before dispatch |
217	| RM-011 | The system shall generate pickup/delivery checklist for operations staff |
218	| RM-012 | The system shall track equipment condition at checkout and check-in |
219	
220	#### 3.2.5 Billing and Invoicing
221	| ID | Requirement Description |
222	|----|------------------------|
223	| BI-001 | The system shall generate invoices based on rental duration, equipment rates, applicable taxes, and additional charges |
224	| BI-002 | The system shall support different billing models: daily, weekly, monthly rates |
225	| BI-003 | The system shall calculate and apply taxes (GST) according to Indian tax regulations |
226	| BI-004 | The system shall support security deposit collection and refund processing |
227	| BI-005 | The system shall generate periodic invoices for ongoing long-term rentals |
228	| BI-006 | The system shall track payment status (pending, paid, partial, overdue) |
229	| BI-007 | The system shall apply late fees for overdue payments per company policy |
230	| BI-008 | The system shall support multiple payment methods: bank transfer, credit card, online payment gateways |
231	| BI-009 | The system shall generate payment receipts for all transactions |
232	| BI-010 | The system shall provide aging reports for accounts receivable |
233	| BI-011 | The system shall allow adjustment of invoices for damages, late returns, or early termination |
234	
235	#### 3.2.6 Maintenance Management
236	| ID | Requirement Description |
237	|----|------------------------|
238	| MM-001 | The system shall track maintenance schedules for all equipment based on manufacturer recommendations or usage |
239	| MM-002 | The system shall allow scheduling of preventive maintenance and track completion |
240	| MM-003 | The system shall manage repair workflows: issue reporting, diagnosis, repair estimation, parts replacement, and completion |
241	| MM-004 | The system shall track warranty claims and coordinate with OEMs for warranty repairs |
242	| MM-005 | The system shall equipment available for rental only after maintenance/repair completion and quality check |
243	| MM-006 | The system shall maintain maintenance history for each equipment item |
244	| MM-007 | The system shall generate maintenance reports and forecasts |
245	
246	#### 3.2.7 Reporting and Analytics
247	| ID | Requirement Description |
248	|----|------------------------|
249	| RA-001 | The system shall provide dashboard showing key metrics: utilization rates, revenue, active rentals, pending maintenance |
250	| RA-002 | The system shall generate utilization reports by equipment type, brand, and model |
251	| RA-003 | The system shall provide revenue reports by time period, customer, and equipment category |
252	| RA-004 | The system shall track customer lifetime value and rental frequency |
253	| RA-005 | The system shall provide aging reports for accounts receivable and equipment maintenance |
254	| RA-006 | The system shall generate equipment lifecycle reports to inform procurement decisions |
255	| RA-007 | The system shall support export of reports in PDF, Excel, and CSV formats |
256	| RA-008 | The system shall provide real-time inventory availability dashboard |
257	
258	#### 3.2.8 Customer Portal
259	| ID | Requirement Description |
260	|----|------------------------|
261	| CP-001 | The customer portal shall allow authenticated customers to browse available inventory with real-time availability |
262	| CP-002 | The customer portal shall allow customers to submit rental requests with equipment selection, quantities, and rental period |
263	| CP-003 | The customer portal shall allow customers to view their current and past rentals |
264	| CP-004 | The customer portal shall allow customers to view and download invoices and payment receipts |
265	| CP-005 | The customer portal shall allow customers to make online payments for invoices |
266	| CP-006 | The customer portal shall allow customers to request rental extensions or early termination |
267	| CP-007 | The customer portal shall provide notifications for upcoming returns, payments, and contract expirations |
268	| CP-008 | The customer portal shall support document upload for KYC and authorization forms |
269	
270	#### 3.2.9 Website Integration
271	| ID | Requirement Description |
272	|----|------------------------|
273	| WI-001 | The system shall provide RESTful API endpoints for the existing website to consume |
274	| WI-002 | The API shall provide real-time inventory availability for display on the website |
275	| WI-003 | The API shall provide product catalog information (specifications, pricing, availability) |
276	| WI-004 | The API shall allow submission of rental inquiries from the website to the RMS |
277	| WI-005 | The API shall authenticate website requests using secure tokens or API keys |
278	| WI-006 | The system shall synchronize product categories and branding with the website |
279	
280	### 3.3 Non-Functional Requirements
281	
282	#### 3.3.1 Performance Requirements
283	| ID | Requirement Description |

285	| PF-001 | The system shall load primary pages within 3 seconds under normal load |
286	| PF-002 | The system shall support concurrent users: 50+ staff users, 100+ customer portal users |
287	| PF-003 | Database queries for inventory search shall return results within 2 seconds |
288	| PF-004 | The system shall generate standard reports within 10 seconds for datasets up to 10,000 records |
289

291	| ID | Requirement Description |

293	| SR-001 | All data transmission shall use HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ encryption |
294	| SR-002 | Passwords shall be stored using strong, salted hashing (bcrypt or equivalent) |
295	| SR-003 | The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) for all functions |
296	| SR-004 | The system shall log all access to sensitive data (customer information, financial data) |

337	### 3.4 Other Requirements
338	
339	#### 3.4.1 Business Rules
340	| ID | Requirement Description |
341	|----|------------------------|

344	| BR-003 | The system shall require security deposit of 20% for equipment valued over ₹50,000 |

353	| CL-003 | The system shall generate GST-compliant invoices with proper HSN/SAC codes |

355	| CL-005 | The system shall support generation of TDS certificates where applicable |
356	
357	## Appendices
358	
359	### Appendix A: Glossary

We need to produce a structured output using StructuredOutput tool with fields: currentState (object with accessibility, cssIssues, htmlStructure, jsFunctionality, performance, responsiveness), improvementAreas (array of strings), srsRequirements (array of strings). We must fill them based on analysis. Let's analyze each aspect. First, HTML structure: review index.html. Observations: - The HTML uses semantic elements: header, nav, section, footer. Good. - There's a logo image with alt text? The logo image src="logo.png" but there's no alt attribute? Actually line 23: `` yes alt present. - There's missing alt for some images: In partners-section, images have alt attributes (e.g., alt="Dell") good. - In services-section, service-card images have alt attributes (e.g., alt="Server Rental") good. - In refurbished products section, there are images with src="images/refurb-laptop.png" alt="Refurbished Laptop" good; however there are images with src="iserver.png" (typo? maybe missing folder) alt="Refurbished Servers" and "Refurbished Computers". The image file may not exist; but alt present. - The hero slider: each slide has an image (banner.png, banner2.png, banner3.jpeg) but no alt attribute? Actually inside slide div, there's `` without alt. That's an accessibility issue: missing alt text for banner images. Also the content inside slide doesn't have headings? There's h1 and p inside .content, which is good. - The navigation: active class on Home link; but there is no aria-current="page"? Not a big issue. - The quote button and other links have href="#" which is okay for placeholder but not accessible for screen readers if they don't lead anywhere; but it's a prototype. - The site uses Font Awesome icons via CDN, which is okay. - There's a missing meta description? Not present; only charset and viewport. Missing meta description for SEO. - No lang attribute on html? Actually lang="en" present. - No skip-to-content link. - Use of aria-labels? Not present. - The slider buttons have no aria-label; they are button elements with only icon inside; need aria-label="Previous slide" etc. - Dots are span elements; they should have role="button" and aria-label? Or use button elements. - The website uses a lot of div; could be improved with more semantic elements (like article, etc.) but overall okay. - The footer contains phone number with tel:+ but missing number? Actually `Call Now` missing number; also in footer contact list there is empty phone number. Thus HTML structure issues: missing alt text for banner images, missing aria-labels for controls, missing meta description, missing skip link, placeholder links with href="#" and missing phone number. CSS issues: Review style.css. Observations: - Uses CSS variables? Not really; uses hardcoded colors. - Uses CSS gradients and transitions; seems okay. - There's duplicate .container definition (line 15 and line 320) - duplicate class definition; later overrides earlier? That's a CSS issue: duplicate class definition. - There's a .section-heading defined twice (lines 326-349 and again lines 440-470). Actually appears twice; second overrides first but duplication. - There's a .section-heading inside .why-choose-section that duplicates earlier .section-heading; causing confusion. - There's a .benefit-section with gradient background but text color white; contrast may be okay. - The site uses fixed height for hero-slider: height:90vh; .slide img height:90vh; object-fit:cover; okay. - There's a .hero class with min-height:100vh; but later .hero-slider overrides? Actually there is .hero (lines 81-89) and .hero-slider (lines 161-166). Might be conflicting. - There's a .hero-content defined but not used? Actually .hero-content appears in CSS lines 91-97 but not used in HTML? The HTML uses .hero-slider .slide .content; not .hero-content. So .hero-content unused. - There's a .hero-text defined but not used. - There's duplicate .section-heading causing confusion. - There's a .benefit-item duplication? Not sure. - There's a missing favicon link. - CSS uses many vendor prefixes? Not needed. - There's a .partner-track animation scrollBrands that moves left -50% (assuming duplicate images). Might cause performance but okay. - Use of backdrop-filter may not be supported in older browsers; but okay. - There's a .why-choose-section::before and ::after with blur filters; may affect performance. Potential CSS issues: duplicate class definitions, unused styles, potential specificity conflicts, lack of CSS custom properties for theming, lack of dark/light mode (though site is dark background). Also no responsive breakpoints defined explicitly; but they use flexbox and grid with auto-fit, which is responsive. Check media queries: none. So responsiveness relies on fluid layouts; may be okay but could be improved with breakpoints. JS functionality: main.js handles slider, intersection observer for why-card fade-in. It's simple. No API integration, no dynamic data loading, no form validation, no rental request handling. The site is static; SRS requires dynamic features like inventory browsing, rental requests, customer portal, etc. So JS functionality is lacking for the required features. Performance: No lazy loading of images; all images load at once. Could use loading="lazy". No minification of CSS/JS (but it's small). No caching headers (server side). No use of CDN for assets besides fonts and Font Awesome. Accessibility: Missing alt text for banner images, missing aria-labels for controls, missing skip link, missing lang attribute on html? Already present. Missing role attributes for slider buttons. Missing focus visible styles? Not defined. Now we need to map to SRS requirements: The SRS outlines many functional requirements: inventory management, customer management, rental management, billing, maintenance, reporting, customer portal, website integration. The current website is just a static front-end with no backend integration. It lacks: - Dynamic inventory display (should pull from API) - Rental request submission via API - Customer login / portal - Real-time availability - Admin/dashboard - etc. Thus improvement areas: implement backend APIs, connect frontend to API, add user authentication, add dynamic content loading, improve accessibility, improve performance (lazy loading, minification), add missing meta tags, fix duplicate CSS, add proper alt text, add aria labels, implement responsive breakpoints, add form validation, etc. Now we need to output via StructuredOutput. Let's craft the JSON. First, currentState: we need to provide strings for each aspect: accessibility, cssIssues, htmlStructure, jsFunctionality, performance, responsiveness. We'll write concise summaries. ImprovementAreas: array of strings describing areas for improvement. SrsRequirements: array of strings describing which SRS requirements are not met or need implementation. We'll need to read the SRS to extract relevant requirements that are missing. But we can summarize. Let's produce output. We'll call StructuredOutput with appropriate fields. But first, maybe we should double-check if there are any other files like server.png etc. Not needed.
